## Intent

- The remote-access stack is four layers with one shape: herdr (0.8.2 against v0.9.0), its Collie plugin (0.32.0 against v1.8.0, a major boundary), the tailnet sidecars (`board` and `viewer` to be removed), and tailscale (app, wrapper, Remote Login, auth key, MagicDNS, HTTPS). Each lives in a `topic-*` memory; README § Procedures carries four planned rows.
- Wanted: one shape, `status|upgrade|up|down <layer>`, on every layer, so one verb reads the stack and another acts on one layer.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/service/` (or one directory per layer over a shared `scripts/lib/service.sh`; the worker picks and says why) covers herdr `upgrade <tag>`; collie `status`, `install`, `upgrade <tag>`, `up`; sidecar `status`, `down <app>`, `recreate <app>`; tailscale `check`. `just --list` names every verb.

- Inside the sub-issue: herdr, then Collie (a herdr plugin), then sidecars, then the tailscale check the other three call first.

request.body:
## Intent

- The `claude-wakeup` row of README § Procedures reads `planned`. Nothing on this Mac brings a session back on a schedule: no `pmset repeat`, no caffeinate agent, no launchd agent that prompts a herdr pane or runs `claude -p`, and the host record's "Services after a login" section says what does not come back.
- Wanted: `status` that reads the three pieces, and `install` that writes them, so an unattended wake is a script and not a memory.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/claude-wakeup/` carries `status` and `install`; `just --list` names both.
- `status` prints `pmset -g sched`, the caffeinate agent's `launchctl print`, and the wakeup agent's plist, schedule and last exit, each with where it was read; one verdict line, exit 0/1/2.
- `install` writes the plists under `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, loads them, is idempotent, refuses a loaded agent without `--force`, and prints the step a person takes (the pmset schedule needs sudo).
- The wakeup agent's action is one of: prompt a named herdr pane, or run `claude -p` with a prompt file; the choice is a `DECISION` on this issue before `install` lands.
- Run live on this Mac with `status` output on the pull request; host record "Services after a login" re-probed; README row reads `landed`; `campaign-installed reach` shows the merge at `~/<campaign>`.

## Plan

- Read `topic-service-runtime` and campaign-base `assuming-role/scripts/campaign-limit-reset.py`, which already schedules a detached prompt after a limit reset; do not duplicate its mechanism.
- Any `herdr` call that drives a pane is guarded by `HERDR_ENV=1` and names its target.
- Independent of the rows before it.

## Intent

- Each phone app (garden, camera today) carries `scripts/release-app.sh` and a `docs/release.md`, but no step reaches the phone: `adb devices` is empty, the phone `R5KL30C9J7B` is intermittent, and "the phone holds the latest release" is never checked. README § Procedures carries it as one planned row.
- Wanted: one procedure for any app with a release script, `app status|release|install <app>`, so what is built, what is released and what the phone runs are three readings of one script.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/app/` carries the three verbs taking an app name; the app list is a host fact (`HOST_APPS`), not a literal in the script; `just --list` names each verb.
- `status <app>` prints the newest `dist/*.apk` in `repos/<app>`, the newest `gh release` tag and asset, and the version the phone reports over `adb -s HOST_PHONE_SERIAL`, each with where it was read; one verdict line, exit 0/1/2, "phone not attached" being exit 2 with the numbered step.
- `release <app>` calls the app's own `scripts/release-app.sh`, never a copy; `install <app>` pushes the released apk, refusing a downgrade without `--force`; a missing clone under `repos/` is cloned.
- Run live on this Mac for garden and camera with `status` output on the pull request; both installed on the phone, or the row names the person's step.
- README row reads `landed`; host record Devices row and `facts.sh` re-probed; `campaign-installed reach` shows the merge at `~/<campaign>`.

## Plan

- Read each app's `docs/release.md` (Scope Out: not edited) and `topic-android-toolchain` for the adb and keystore traps.
- After <campaign>#321, which pins the JDK and adb the release needs.

request.body:
## Intent

- The `macos-automation` row of README § Procedures reads `planned`. Which context may drive System Events on this Mac — a terminal, a launchd agent, a herdr pane — is known only by trying it, and a probe that hangs on a consent dialog has no bound.
- Wanted: `check`, a read-only verb that answers, per context, whether Automation consent is granted, bounded by an external kill so it never hangs a session.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/macos-automation/check.sh` runs a harmless `osascript` against System Events under a timeout it starts itself, prints the context it ran in, the TCC verdict it read (`tccutil` is write-only, so the verdict is the probe's exit and message), and the consent step a person takes as a numbered instruction; one verdict line, exit 0/1/2.
- The kill is external to the probe (`timeout`-style wrapper or a background `sleep; kill`), and the script says so beside the bound.
- Run live on this Mac from a terminal and from a herdr pane with both outputs on the pull request; the host record gains a row for the verdict per context.
- `just --list` names `macos-automation-check`; README row reads `landed`; `campaign-installed reach` shows the merge at `~/<campaign>`.

## Plan

- Last of the eight rows; depends on nothing, and claude-wakeup's launchd agent is the third context to probe once it exists.
- Never trigger a modal dialog from inside a session unbounded: the wrapper's timeout is set before the first run.
- Traps true of any Mac stay in a `topic-*` memory; only this Mac's verdicts go to `hosts/`.

request.body:
## Intent

- Owner's question (2026-09-12): buy a second Mac mini, set it up from `kalaluthien/<campaign>` alone -- possible? If not, what is missing? Of the missing pieces, which are environment setup rather than secrets? What would expressing those as gitops take?
- Today `hosts/hyungs-mac-mini/` records one machine and every script reads it; nothing separates what the machine is from what was done to it, so nobody can say what a fresh machine would still lack.

## Definition of done

- One NOTE on this issue holding: (a) an inventory of what a second Mac mini would need, one row each, tagged `in repo` / `env, not in repo` / `secret`, with the evidence for each row (a file, a probe, a command output from this Mac -- never memory); (b) for the `env, not in repo` rows, 2-3 gitops shapes (what is declared where, what reconciles it, what runs it), each with trade-offs, one recommended; (c) the hypotheses explored and each one's verdict.
- Every hypothesis run by its own subagent, in parallel, model named on each launch, each returning a table the worker merges.
- Closed by a planner `DECISION` naming the shape that goes on to a development sub-issue. Lands no commit.

## Plan

- Step 1 (now): post a NOTE listing the candidate hypotheses -- at least: `hosts/ + scripts/ suffice`; `~/.dotfiles` carries the rest`; `Brewfile covers the tools`; `launchd agents and login items are unrecorded`; `Docker, Tailscale, Collie state is per machine`; `~/.claude and memory pool are setup, not secret`; `secrets: keychain, ssh, auth keys, gh`; stop and wait for the planner's pick.
- Step 2: fan out one subagent per picked hypothesis; merge into the inventory NOTE.
- Step 3: the gitops shapes NOTE. Then the planner decides.
- Constraints: change no code; read `~/<campaign>`, `~/.dotfiles`, `~/.claude`, and this Mac live; a `secret` row names the store, never the value.
- Related: the services-reconcile sub-issue reads this inventory's `env` rows.

## Lands in

- kalaluthien/<campaign>

## Intent

- Owner's question (2026-09-12): what must this Mac keep serving, and what must run on a cycle and reconcile drift? ## Intent

- Owner's word, 2026-09-13 (DECISION on <campaign>#229, issuecomment-5647204384): every campaign surveys its own Scope for maintenance that is possible and missing, then carries every finding out.

## Definition of done

- A finding with no readable evidence is not a row. A finding whose fix would change what the campaign IS (its Scope, a rule found two incompatible ways, a destructive step) is a `BLOCKED` on this issue, not a row.
- Every quality swept, and a quality with no finding says so with what was read.
- Closed by a planner `DECISION` listing the follow-ups to reopen or file. Lands no commit.

## Plan

- Read `campaign-tracker.py index 229` first: the closed list is what `reopen <campaign>#N` points at.

- Step 2: merge into one table, drop rows without evidence, dedupe a finding two lenses share, tag each row's follow-up against the index; post the NOTE; stop and wait for the planner's DECISION.
- Constraints: change no code; a `BLOCKED` for anything that would move the Scope; read files, never memory.

## Intent

- The scenario–test–code tie is a rule a machine can decide, and today nothing decides it: a commit that adds code with no scenario, or a scenario no test names, passes every guard.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/check-sdlc-tie.py` refuses a commit whose staged change breaks the tie the model states, prints what it read and which branch it took, and permits loudly on an unforeseen failure.

- `scripts/check-sdlc-tie-test.py` holds one named failing case per refusal branch, and each fails when its branch is deleted from the check.
- `install-hooks.sh` chains it into `pre-commit`; `campaign-primitives.py` lists it; `check.yml` runs its test.
- The pull request is merged, and the `REPORT` quotes one refusal the check printed on a real counterexample.

## Plan

- Waits on the model sub-issue's merge; the tie and the skip rule are read from `spec/sdlc`, and the check's docstring cites them.
- Read `check-tree-shape.py` for the shape of a refusing guard here, and `feedback-guard-tests` in the memory pool for how a refusal is tested.
- Start with the narrowest decidable tie — a scenario name appearing in a test name and a test name in the code path's test — and widen only when a named case demands it.
- Constraint: the check reads names, never verdicts; a solver verdict stays the solver's.

- Two follow-ups #246 left for the next sub-issue touching `scripts/` (NOTE on #246): widen `check-cross-references.py` `ABSOLUTE_PREFIXES` from `spec/campaign/` to `spec/`, with a case in its suite; teach `alloy-check.py --digest` the sdlc signatures (`LETTER`) and relations (`VARYING`), so an sdlc trace digests to more than its events.

- After <campaign>#246's current round lands, since it edits the same Stage comment and deletes `spec/sdlc/diagram.html`.

request.body:
## Intent

- The `check` job's solver step runs every `spec/**/*.als` serially and is the whole wait on a pull request: run 34646154482 on main at 8778b40 spent 48.1 min in it; every other step under 3 min.
- Two modules are 69% of it: `spec/sdlc/checks.als` 21.8 min, `spec/sdlc/scenarios.als` 11.3 min; then `orchestration/scenarios.als` 8.7, `orchestration/checks.als` 3.9; the other 14 under 2 min together.
- pr#306 widened the sdlc model and a pull request's step went from about 24 to about 58 min; the owner asked on 2026-09-12 that it come down.
- A pull request touching only `scripts/` or one entity still pays for every entity: nothing keys a module's result to its content.

## Definition of done

- On a pull request touching no `spec/` module the step is under 5 min, and on one touching one entity it is bounded by that entity's modules; both measured on a real run, quoted with the run id in the REPORT.
- Every `expect` clause is still enforced on main at every merge: no command is skipped whose module, or a module it opens, changed, and the mechanism says what it read and which modules it ran.
- A per-module solver-time floor is recorded, so the next widening is seen when it lands.
- The pull request is merged and the install shows it.

## Plan

- Measure first: per-module seconds from the run log become a checked-in table or a step output.
- Two levers, in order; add the second only if the first misses the target:
  1. Run an entity's modules only when its content, or a module it `open`s, differs from the last green main run: key on a hash of the closure, never on the git diff, and run everything on main.
  2. Fan the step out into a matrix job per entity so the wall time is the slowest entity, not the sum.
- Shrinking the sdlc scopes is a model change for a sub-issue of its own; this one changes no `.als`.
- Constraint: the snapshot step, `alloy-check.py`'s dead-event refusal and `check-merge-review.py`'s step stay.

## Lands in

- none

## Intent

- `spec/sdlc` carries a `Docs` stage the tree already breaks: `docs/` is gone (de55550) and 13 of 102 `spec/` commits since added a `sig` and landed; `landDiscipline` has no reader (review F1).
- `AddsShape` has no decidable subject: `system.als:52` and `:127` disagree on what a Spec artifact is (F2). `rewrite`/`replace` reach no command (F3).
- Model `tieDiscipline` is whole-tree while `check-sdlc-tie.py` enforces a delta plus a 20-entry `LEGACY` list: 20 of 31 code paths untied, guard green (F4).
- Findings: planner's review set, `scratchpad/spec-review/review-sdlc.md`, summarized in this issue's first NOTE.

## Definition of done

- One merged pull request: `spec/sdlc/` is `system.als` + `checks.als`, `scenarios.als` merged into `checks.als`; `Docs`, `AddsShape`, `rewrite`, `replace` deleted; `var sig Licensed in Artifact` added, `everyCodeHasScenario` quantifies over `Written & stage.Code - Licensed`, `Licensed` never grows, with its `_Bites` run.
- `check-sdlc-tie.py` reads scenario names from `spec/commands.snapshot.json` instead of importing `DECL` from `alloy-check.py`; `LEGACY` is what `Licensed` names.
- Every command keeps its `expect`; snapshot regenerated; CI green. Local solve of the merged `checks.als` measured by the planner at 188 s against 570 s today; the pull request's REPORT quotes its own measurement.
- `kind-prototyping.md:36` reads `optional = Spec`; `landing-a-change.md` Docs rows deleted.

## Plan

- Read the finding list first: `review-sdlc.md` F1-F5 as pasted in NOTE 1.
- Order: model cut, then reader change, then prose, one commit each; open the pull request on the first commit.
- Off limits: `spec/campaign/**` (another sub-issue), `check-tree-shape.py` (the tooling sub-issue lands after the campaign moves).
- `SkipReadAtTheTimeIsNotEnough` retargets to `Spec` (its criterion reads `writtenOf`, which grows) or is deleted with a one-line reason in the REPORT.

## Intent

- Nothing checks that a script decides what the model says: `check-sdlc-tie.py` ties a scenario to a test by NAME only, 25 suites run on hand-written fixtures, and no reader compares a script's verdict with the predicate it claims to implement.
- Evidence it matters: sdlc F4, where the model's `tieDiscipline` and its reader disagreed on 20 of 31 code paths while CI stayed green.
- Steps 1 and 2 (NOTEs on this issue) showed a witness's solver instance yields a fixture the suite runs, and that the model's own story fails the suite exactly when the model's relation says so. The DECISION names the shape.

## Definition of done

- One merged pull request: `alloy-check.py --digest` prints the file's own `var` relations beside the events; `check-merge-review-test.py` gains one case whose fixture is derived by an in-suite adapter from the digest of `M2_MergeInTheStateAfterAPush`, the sha rule stated once in the adapter, the expected word derived from `Reviewed` at the merge state; the case fails when the adapter's relation reading is flipped.
- The REPORT names which of the 25 suites name a witness today and could take the same adapter, without building them.

## Plan

- Lands after <campaign>#341, whose pull request moves `check-sdlc-tie.py`'s scenario reading; rebase on it.
- Generic part first (digest), adapter second, one commit each; no converter over every suite.
- Scratch under `scratch-342/` is the worked example; nothing from it is committed as is.

## Intent

- `spec/sdlc/system.als` models one shape of change: a feature added or changed, where every stage's artifact is new and `feeds` orders them Intent -> Plan -> Spec -> Test -> Code.
- A change that adds no behaviour has no home: strengthening a test suite, raising code quality, a refactor that keeps every scenario and witness as it is. Its Spec artifact is the existing one it reuses, and the rule it must keep is that no witness or scenario leaves and no `LEGACY` entry grows.
- The owner asked for this on 2026-09-13; nothing today refuses such a change, and nothing says what it owes.

## Definition of done

- One merged pull request in which `spec/sdlc` names the no-feature change -- a profile, a kind, or a fact over the existing `Change` -- with a check that a hardening change may not drop a witness or add a `LEGACY` path, its `_Bites` witness, and a `Cov_` run.
- The kind reference or `AGENTS.md` profile line that derives from it, and `check-sdlc-tie.py` reading whatever the model makes checkable, each with a failing case.
- The REPORT lists the three simplicity counts before and after (files, commands, guard rules).

## Plan

- Exploratory: the planner drives it step by step with a separate worker, one DECISION per step on this issue.
- Step 1: read the model after <campaign>#341 and #343 land and propose two shapes (a profile with `optional = Spec` reusing the existing witness, or a `Hardening` change with its own fact), each with its check named; post as BLOCKED.
- Constraint: strictly simpler or equal on the #244 DECISION's three measures; no new stage.

## Intent

- `spec/sdlc/system.als` has three events, `Write`, `Rename`, `Land`, and none that removes an artifact: a scenario, witness or code path that no longer earns its place has no lifecycle step, so nothing says when it dies, who decides, or what the tie guard does with the hole.
- Owner, 2026-09-14: model "dead spec/code elimination" as one lifecycle scenario of `spec/sdlc`, and say how it reaches the scripts (`check-sdlc-tie`, `alloy-check --commands`, the snapshot) and the agents (worker procedure, planner survey).
- Owner, same day: death is one of several failure modes -- orphan (dead), mismatch (tied to the wrong thing), unspecified (code with no spec), undefined (a name nothing defines), and others found -- each specified cleanly, as one shape.
- <campaign>#343 round 2, the dead-rule survey over `spec/`, is the live instance and this research's material.

## Definition of done

- A `DECISION` here with: (1) the failure-mode table: mode, meaning in model terms (`Written`, `Licensed`, `tie`, `witnesses`), caught today by what, or by nothing; (2) 2-3 candidate shapes for the missing ones (an `Unwrite` event, a `Dead` state, a `Change` kind), each judged by what the model checks, what a script refuses, what an agent does differently; (3) one recommendation; (4) <campaign>#343 evidence: the mode of each dead row, how found, which a check could have made.
- The DECISION names follow-ups, `kind:development`, one mechanism each; this issue closes with no pull request.
- Out: writing the model.

## Plan

- Read <campaign>#343's round-2 DECISION and NOTEs as they land; keep the planner's script (NOTE 2) as `<campaign>/scripts/spec-dead-count.py`, probe 1, and record what it could and could not decide.
- Draft the table and shapes against `spec/sdlc/system.als` and `scripts/check-sdlc-tie.py`; per shape, name the guard branch and the agent step it changes.
- Judge by the three simplicity counts; post the DECISION; file follow-ups; close.

## Intent

## Intent

- A worker that authored a pull request launches its own review subagent (reviewing.md, feedback-review-roles) and posts the `REVIEW` it returns. Claude Code's auto-mode permission check refuses that `gh pr comment` as self-approval: tidy-dotclaude#413 BLOCKED, 2026-09-14, dotclaude pr#30 at b83e9c1, no findings, unposted. Merge condition 1 then cannot be met from the worker's pane.
- Owner (tidy-dotclaude#413 DECISION, 2026-09-14): it happens often; <campaign> designs the fix. The interim is a fresh reviewer session per pull request, one launch each.

request.body:
## Intent

- Merge condition 1 — a review read at the sha being merged — has no reader: pr#262 merged at 8ca2609 with zero comments opening `REVIEW` and zero pull-request reviews (NOTE on <campaign>#247, 2026-09-09), and nothing refused it. `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions says as much: "condition 1 is readable and read by nothing".
- A `REPORT` that pins a sha other than the head is the same gap from the other side: the review it asks for is at a sha nobody will merge.
- Reopened 2026-09-10: a posted `REVIEW` fires no workflow, so every merge waits on a hand `gh run rerun` (baseline#1 friction list).

## Definition of done

- `scripts/check-merge-review.py <pr>` reads the pull request's head sha and its comments, and refuses when no comment opening `REVIEW` names that sha; it prints the head, every `REVIEW` sha it read, and which branch it took; an unreadable pull request is `could not look`, not a pass.
- The same script, given a `REPORT` comment body, refuses one whose sha is not the head.
- Its suite has one named failing case per refusal branch, pr#262's shape among them, each failing when its branch is deleted.
- `campaign-claim.py release` calls it before deleting a merged claim's ref and refuses on its verdict; `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs it as a required status on the pull request head, so a merge without a `REVIEW` at that sha is refused by GitHub.
- `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions replaces "read by nothing" with the mechanism's name.
- Posting a `REVIEW` re-runs `check` on that head with no hand step; `check.yml`'s re-run note is gone.

## Plan

- Read `check-campaign-claim.py`'s `COMMENT_CEILING` block for how a `REVIEW` first line is parsed today; reuse it, do not restate it.
- Script and suite first; then the `release` hook; then CI; then the prose. One commit each so reviews narrow.
- Constraint: the script reads GitHub through `gh`, never a pane or a transcript.

- none

## Intent

- Three `AGENTS.md` rules were prose the guard could hold, each with an incident; landed in pr#281 (the refusals) and pr#355 (one home for every review statement).
- Reopened 2026-09-16 for a fourth: a recursive search rooted at the home folder, or at a folder macOS guards, hangs on a permission prompt charged to herdr (the reopen NOTE), and the Bash reader allows it unread.

## Definition of done

- The Bash reader refuses a walking command -- `find`, `bfs`, `fd`, `rg`, `grep -r`/`-R`, `du`, `tree`, `ls -R` -- whose positional path argument is `~`, `$HOME` or `Path.home()`, or is one of or lies under `~/Pictures`, `~/Music`, `~/Movies`, `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, `~/Downloads`. The refusal names the verb and the root it read. `find ~/campaign-base` passes, and so does a non-walking command on a file there (`cat ~/Documents/x.md`).
- `Glob` and `Grep` join the matcher, and their `path` field is read by the same rule; a missing `path` passes.
- Named failing cases, each failing with its branch deleted: `find /Users/hyungmokim -maxdepth 4 -name CLAUDE.local.md` (planner-10, 2026-09-15 14:48) and a `Glob` whose `path` is `~/Downloads`.
- A python `glob` in a heredoc stays a named gap in the docstring: a heredoc body is data (baseline#193).
- `guard-corpus.py` replay over the recorded allows refuses the `find` call above and nothing else; the reviewer's heredoc glob stays allowed as the gap named above, and the REPORT gives the counts.
- The tccd fact (`responsible=` herdr, the grant keyed on herdr's Cellar path) sits in the docstring beside the rule; `AGENTS.md` § Watching and retiring gains one clause naming the mechanism.

## Plan

- One commit for the Bash rule and its cases, one for the matcher and the two tool fields, one for the prose; each review narrowed to its diff.
- Constraint: every refusal prints what it read, and the last-resort handler still permits.

## Intent

- In baseline#289 a `Where.machine` condition made the new `Handoff` event impossible to reach, and four `check`s about it passed without testing anything (baseline#1 friction list, <campaign>#272 NOTE). Nothing refused it; a reviewer caught it one round late.
- An Alloy `check` over an event nothing can fire holds vacuously. That can be decided by machine, so it belongs to a script and not to a reviewer's attention.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/alloy-check.py` refuses a model where an event a `check` names cannot fire: every such event has a satisfiable witness `run`, and an unsatisfiable or missing one is a refusal naming the event and the file.
- It prints which events it read, which witness it ran for each, and the verdict; a model it could not run is `could not look`, not a pass.
- Its suite has a named failing case per refusal branch: the baseline#289 shape (an event unreachable because of a `Where` condition) among them, each failing when its branch is removed.
- Every model under `spec/` passes, or each one that fails is fixed in the same pull request; `check` green; merged.

## Plan

- Read the `topic-alloy` memory (the witness that passes without testing its rule) and `alloy-check.py --commands` before designing the witness.
- Derive the event list from the declarations, not from comments.
- Off limits: the models' semantics. A model that now fails gets its witness fixed, not its rule weakened.

## Intent

- The heartbeat is a planner-side poller (1,221 + 1,896 test lines, 29 commits 09-10..09-14) that reads other sessions' screens and transcripts to decide what each could decide itself. 2026-09-14 it failed four ways: <campaign>'s watch died unnoticed, <campaign> ran none, <campaign> skipped `--apply`, <campaign> wrote its own wrapper.
- Owner, 2026-09-14: develop two different replacements, decide by experiment; backlog until the owner lifts it. Interim: the restarting watch in NOTE on <campaign>#272.

## Definition of done

- A closing `DECISION`: option table opened by purpose and blocker, lenses reliability / complexity / fit with standing decisions (no cron, one wake, prompts into panes), one recommendation; the owner picks, the build is filed after.
- Each option's experiment NOTE fills one matrix: watch dead, no watch, skipped apply, permission prompt, usage limit, crash or exit, context >= 250k, finished worker, planner compacted or switched. Every cell names its evidence.

## Plan

- **P, sessions push**: `--autocompact 250k` at launch; worker hooks on `StopFailure`, `Notification` (permission prompt) and `SessionEnd` prompt the planner's pane; the final `REPORT` (<campaign>#436) drives the retire; Claude Code's quota auto-resume covers a limit. The watch is deleted.
- **S, one supervisor**: one process outside every session per bound campaign runs the readings and the fixed verdicts (fire, compact, retire, quiet) and prompts the planner only for drift needing judgement. The Monitor rule is deleted.
- Probes first, each able to fail: where `--autocompact 250k` compacts; `StopFailure` `rate_limit` and quota auto-resume at the next real limit; a hook prompting a pane through herdr; a launchd process reaching herdr's socket.
- Throwaway sessions only; live campaigns untouched. Count lines added and removed, and the spec's three measures.
- Driven step by step: each NOTE, then stop for the planner.

## Intent

- Four machinery defects campaign #244 surfaced, each recorded where found and fixed by nothing:
  - `campaign-tracker settlement <N>` reports every campaign's claims as `could not look` (NOTE on #1): `campaign-tracker.py:932` calls `all_refs` without the slug; since #237 `prefixes()` returns `[]` without one.
  - `campaign-assign.py` cannot see a release its pane shows (NOTE on #1): its pane read returns 62 lines where `herdr pane read --lines 1000` returns 530.
  - `alloy-check.py --commands <dir> --write` writes a stray snapshot under any directory (NOTE on #250, 17:58Z), which CI never reads and tree-shape never refuses.
  - `check-cross-references.py` reads no `.html` source and only the `spec/campaign/` prefix (NOTE on #250, 22:40Z), so every `.src` pin in both diagrams and every `spec/sdlc/` path is unread.

## Definition of done

- Each of the four is fixed in its script with one named failing case in that script's suite, the case failing when the fix is reverted.
- `settlement 244` names the claim refs of a campaign with a slug; `campaign-assign.py` reads the release and compaction lines of a pane that has them, or says how many lines it read and why that is not enough.
- `--commands` resolves the snapshot root as a constant and refuses another `<dir>`; `check-cross-references.py` reads `.html` sources and the `spec/` prefix, and the probe in the NOTE on #250 reports both paths dangling.
- Every `*-test.*` suite and the four tree guards green; the pull request merged.

## Plan

- Read the four NOTEs first; each names the line and a probe.
- One commit per script, in the order above; run `scripts/campaign-primitives.py` last to confirm every script still lists.
- Constraint: `check-cross-references.py` gaining `.html` will read the pins in `spec/campaign/diagram.html` and `spec/sdlc/diagram.html`; a pin that turns out stale is fixed in this pull request, since the reader that now sees it is this one.

## Intent

- A campaign with nothing left to do keeps its heartbeat running: the planner's `--watch` polls every 60s, and the planner sits idle at full context. Measured 2026-09-12: `<campaign>-planner-1` is the only session of <campaign>#229, every sub-issue is settled (15/15), and its watch still runs.
- Nothing names that state. `campaign-heartbeat.py`'s verdicts (<campaign>#296) act on workers and limits; the planner's own quiet is read by nobody.
- Owner, 2026-09-12: automate it, or state it explicitly — the watch stops and the planner compacts.

## Definition of done

- `campaign-heartbeat.py <N> --watch` prints one line, `quiet <slug>`, and exits 0 when all three hold, each read from the source it already reads: no session of the campaign is listed but the own pane; no open sub-issue lacks `backlog`; no claim ref stands. The line says which three readings it made.
- `campaign-heartbeat.py <N> --apply` on a quiet campaign gives the own pane the verdict `quiet` and sends it `/compact`; without `--apply` it prints `would send`. Any reading that could not be made is `keep`, as today.
- `planner.md` § The planner's clock says what follows `quiet`: the watch has exited and is not restarted; the planner compacts and waits for a person's prompt; the next assignment starts the watch again.
- The suite has one named failing case per new branch — quiet, and each of the three conditions failing alone — each failing when its branch is removed.
- A planner is never sent `/exit`: a campaign always has one.

## Plan

- Read the header of `campaign-heartbeat.py` first: the sources, `transcript_reading`, and why the own pane is skipped for `idle`. Add the readings to the watch's snapshot; do not open a second reader of herdr, the index or the refs.
- `backlog` is read the way `drift unclaimed` reads it.
- Off limits: the guard, `campaign-claim.py`, the merge conditions.

campaigns.rule-check:
In:

- Refuse: a merge with no `REVIEW` at its sha, a `REPORT` off the head, then every `AGENTS.md` sentence a script can decide, costliest first.
- Bound: what a reviewer may spawn and a subagent may signal, held by a guard, not a brief.
- Keep: the base's rules and their readers -- `AGENTS.md`, `spec/campaign/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/skills/`, the hooks -- one home per rule and one reader per reading, a defect in one included (owner, 2026-09-13; #358's survey).

Out:

- The SDLC itself (`spec/sdlc`, `check-sdlc-tie`): #244's.
- The harness's own settings: the owner's; recorded, not changed.
campaigns.sdlc-alloy:
In:

- `spec/sdlc`, an entity of `spec/` in the shape every other entity has, checked and run in CI the way they are; it opens only what it needs of `spec/campaign`.
- The worker's procedure as an `assuming-role` reference, and the sub-issue kind that carries it.
- A `pre-commit` check that refuses a change whose spec, test and code do not tie.
- Since 2026-09-12 (DECISION on this issue): all of `spec/` -- every `spec/campaign` entity included -- and the scripts, guards and CI that keep it honest, for the simplification chosen there.

Out:

- Sessions outside a campaign: reaching them from `~/.claude` is a successor campaign on dotclaude, filed after this one closes.

request.body:
## Intent

- Owner, 2026-09-13, to every planner (DECISION on <campaign>#272, issuecomment-5647204169): survey the campaign's Scope for maintenance that is possible and missing, then carry every finding out. This is <campaign>'s survey; the follow-ups are separate sub-issues.
- <campaign>'s Scope is the base's own rules and their readers: `AGENTS.md`, `spec/campaign/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/skills/`, the hooks. Six qualities judge it: modularity, encapsulation, simplification, unification, structural completeness, cognitive brevity.

## Definition of done

- A table on this issue, one row per finding: the module or document; the quality it fails; evidence a check can read (a rule stated in two places, both cited; a reader with no consumer; a script two skills copy; a count from `campaign-primitives.py` or `check-rule-readers`); the follow-up, `reopen <slug>#N` with the closed sub-issue that covers it (`campaign-tracker index 272`) or `new`. A finding without such evidence is not a row.
- One `BLOCKED` per finding whose fix would change what the campaign IS: its Scope, a rule found two incompatible ways, a destructive step. The survey changes no rule and lands no code.
- A NOTE closing the survey names the follow-ups in landing order, one line each: number or `new <title>`, the rows it takes, the open sub-issues of #272 it waits on (#349, #278, #354, #356 now).
- Closes as completed with no pull request.

## Plan

- Read `campaign-primitives.py`'s full listing and `check-rule-readers.py`'s header first; both count what the base already decides by machine. Read AGENTS.md whole, once.
- Per quality, one pass, cheapest instrument: `grep -c`, `git log -S`, `wc`, the primitives listing; a Python script under the campaign's `scripts/` for a count that repeats.
- Off limits: filing the follow-ups; that is the planner's, from the NOTE.

## Lands in

- none

## Intent

- Round 1 (pr#288): titles capped at 40, slugs at 10 (owner, 2026-09-10). `TITLE_CEILING` in `scripts/campaign-tracker.py`, `SLUG_CEILING` in `campaign-name-session.py`, each the one home of its number.

- Round 1, landed: `SLUG_CEILING` 10, `TITLE_CEILING` 40 with their pinning cases; the template's title comment; every open issue retitled under 40.

- `campaign-tracker.py` imports the constant and is not edited. No spent slug is changed, `<campaign>` included.

## Plan

- One commit on a fresh topic ref under this number: the constant, its comment, the two cases.
- Off limits: `campaign-tracker.py`, the guard, every label on GitHub.
- The pull request carries `Closes kalaluthien/campaign-base#285`.

request.body:
## Intent

worktrees/<issue>-<topic>`), not under `<campaign>/repos/`. Two readers do not see it:
  - `scripts/check-commit-claim.py` reads only base trees and campaign directories. Committing `f3b72ac` on `<campaign>/380-manual` in `~/<campaign>/.worktrees/380-manual` printed `is in no base tree and no campaign directory ... So the commit gate refuses nothing for <campaign>; only no-main-commits bites.
  - `scripts/check-campaign-claim.py` licenses a `gh pr` write by `git worktree list` of the cwd's repository. From the base root a planner's reviewer subagent cannot post a REVIEW on a <campaign> PR, and once ALLOWED one off an unrelated <campaign> worktree (false allow, `runtime/guard.log`, <campaign> pr#21).
- The install is named in the campaign issue's `## Repos` entry as `(installed: <path>, apply: <command>)`, so both readers can find it.

## Definition of done

- `check-commit-claim.py --staged` in a worktree of an installed member repo whose branch is a claim says `claim`; on a non-claim branch there it refuses. A test case for each.
- `check-campaign-claim.py` reads the claims of every installed repo's worktrees (`campaign-repos.py`'s installed marker) beside the base's, so a `gh pr` write on a member repo is licensed by that repo's own claim and never by another repo's worktree. A corpus case for the false allow.
- Merged; `campaign-installed.py reach` line quoted in the REPORT.

## Plan

- Read the campaign's `## Repos` through `campaign-repos.py` for installed paths; treat each install as a checkout root the same way the base is.
- Commit gate: add the install and its linked worktrees to the trees it judges.
- Guard: license a member-repo `gh pr` write only from a worktree list whose repository owns that PR's remote.

## Lands in

- none

## Intent

- Owner, 2026-09-13: when a session ends through a close or any other leave, `claude` exits but the herdr pane and its tab stay open. The script must end all three at once.
- Today only one path does: `campaign-close.py worker` sends `/exit`, waits until the agent is gone, then `herdr tab close` (spec `orchestration/system.als` beside `exitSession`). Every other leave stops at `/exit`:
  - a successor's `/exit` to its predecessor (`assuming-role/references/planner.md` and `worker.md`, step 4);
  - a session leaving by itself: a finished worker, a peer planner, the campaign planner after `campaign-close.py campaign --close`; the brief's "stop the pane".

## Definition of done

- One step in `scripts/campaign-close.py` owns the leave: given a pane, `/exit`, wait until it leaves `herdr agent list`, close its tab; the existing refusal when another pane shares the tab stays.
- A session can run it on itself: a scope such as `campaign-close.
- Every leave path names that step and none says bare `/exit`: `planner.md`, `worker.md`, the assuming-role brief, `AGENTS.md`, the spec comment.
- A failing test per path in `campaign-close-test.py`; suites green; `check-rule-readers`, `check-cross-references` 0.

## Plan

| step | what |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | probe herdr: `herdr pane current` from inside a pane; whether `herdr tab close <own tab>` run detached from that pane completes; record the reading in the PR body |
| 2 | factor `worker`'s exit/gone/tab into one function; add the self scope on it |
| 3 | rewrite the two handover steps and the self-leave sentences to call it |
| 4 | spec comment + tests + REPORT |

- Never: kill in any spelling; bypass a hook; touch `check-campaign-claim.py` or `standing`.
- One PR, `Closes kalaluthien/campaign-base#<this>`.

request.body:
## Intent

- Nothing counts what reading files costs a campaign: `campaign-token-tally.py tool-echo` counts only this repository's scripts' output, not the Read tool or a `cat`/`sed -n`/`head`/`tail` result by file, by size, or by re-read.
- Spotify's Portal (engineering.atspotify.com, 2026-09) saved ~90% by routing reads over 350 lines to a cheap model. Whether that pays here is unknown until the reads are counted; the count decides whether a follow-up builds it.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/campaign-token-tally.py reads` exists, over the same corpus, window and attribution as the other subcommands, printing per file: result bytes of every Read tool result and shell read, reads, re-reads of the same file in one session, and over-threshold or not (one flag, default 350 lines); a per-session table; one summary line: reads' share of all tool-result bytes, and over-threshold and re-read shares of read bytes.
- Every count prints beside its set; an unsplittable result is a floor line, as `tool-echo` does.
- A `NOTE` on this issue holds the method, the window, this machine and the raw tables, and ends with one verdict by a rule written before the run: over-threshold plus re-read bytes at or above 30% of read bytes says build the routing step, below says stop.
- A case in `scripts/campaign-token-tally-test.py` fails first on a fixture with one Read, one `sed -n` and one re-read, then passes.

## Plan

- Share `scan_script_calls`'s transcript walk; no second reader of the grouping.
- A shell read: first word `cat`, `head`, `tail`, or `sed` with `-n`; nothing else.
- The file: the Read tool's `file_path`, or the shell command's last path argument; no path counts as unsplittable.
- Lines from the file on disk when it exists, else from the result; the table says which.
- Write the threshold and the 30% rule in the docstring before running; run over 2026-09-01 to the run date; post the `NOTE`.
- No hook, no routing script, no skill: measure only.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- A worker is assigned by one sentence naming the sub-issue, and reads the body. The DECISION, NOTE, BLOCKED and REVIEW comments on that issue, on the issues and pull requests its body cites, and the campaign issue's NOTEs naming it (carried items, earlier verdicts) reach it only if the planner points at them. Nothing gathers them, so a worker re-reads threads by hand or misses one (owner, 2026-09-14).

## Definition of done

- `scripts/campaign-context.py <issue> [owner/repo]` prints, through `gh` alone, in one fixed order: the issue's own kind-opening comments (`DECISION`, `NOTE`, `BLOCKED`, `REVIEW`, `REPORT`) oldest first; then, one hop, the `DECISION` and `NOTE` comments of each `<slug>#N` and the `REVIEW` comments of each `pr#N` the body or those comments cite; then the parent campaign issue's `NOTE` and `DECISION` comments naming this issue. A row: kind, author, date, comment id, first line, body under a per-comment cap; one ceiling overall, with a line saying how many rows were cut and where the full thread is.
- Every section says what it read and from where; an empty section prints as empty; a failed `gh` read prints `unread` for that section and exits non-zero.
- `campaign-assign.py`'s prompt adds: run `scripts/campaign-context.py <issue>` first. The prompt stays one sentence; no file is written.
- `assuming-role/references/worker.md` says to run it before the body.
- A test over fixture `gh` JSON on `PATH` fails first on: one own DECISION, one cited `pr#N` REVIEW, one campaign NOTE naming the issue, one comment over the cap.

## Plan

- Reuse `campaign-tracker.py`'s `gh` call shape; import the kind-line grammar from `check-campaign-claim.py`, do not restate it.
- Citations are `<slug>#N` and `pr#N` as `AGENTS.md` § Sub-issues spells them; a bare `#N` is not followed.
- Ceilings are two constants, each printed beside its measurement.
- Name and placement through the `filing` skill. Full review at the first sha, Opus high.

- The owner's order of 2026-09-14 ("every planner on Fable hands off to an Opus high planner", <campaign>#245 comment 5659188284) moved by hand: one peer read every transcript, one message per planner.
- Nothing in `spec/campaign/` names one instruction addressed to every session of a role at once, and no script delivers one: `campaign-assign.py` and `herdr agent prompt` address one pane each.
- The owner asked (same comment) that the scenario be specified or built into the harness, so one short instruction moves every planner.

## Definition of done

- `spec/campaign/session/system.als` or `orchestration/system.als` models a fleet-wide instruction: one owner word, delivered to every listed session of the named role, with the hand-off it demands (successor launched on the named model, state handed over, the old session leaving by `leave`).
- One script reads `herdr agent list`, filters by role and, where asked, by the model read from each transcript, and prompts each matching pane with the instruction; it prints what it read, whom it addressed, whom it skipped and why.
- The prompt names `planner.md` § Handing off (already written, model `handoff`), never restates it; `launching.md`'s model table no longer pins the planner to Fable.
- A merged pull request lands all of it, reviewed at its sha; `check-rule-readers` passes.

## Plan

- Run `scripts/campaign-context.py <this issue>` first; read the owner comment and `planner.md` § The planner's clock.
- Step 1, the spec: add the scenario, strictly simpler on the three counted measures (a field before a new sig).
- Step 2, the script, `--dry-run` first (lists targets, prompts nothing). Model read from the transcript's last assistant `model`; no transcript reads `unknown` and is skipped.
- Step 3: the model table in `launching.md`, one line, and the reference the prompt cites.
- Pull request on the first commit; the worker runs its own review (Opus high) and posts REVIEW at the sha.

## Lands in

- none

In:

- Refuse: a merge with no `REVIEW` at its sha, a `REPORT` off the head, then every `AGENTS.md` sentence a script can decide, costliest first.
- Bound: what a reviewer may spawn and a subagent may signal, held by a guard, not a brief.
- Keep: the base's rules and their readers -- `AGENTS.md`, `spec/campaign/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/skills/`, the hooks -- one home per rule and one reader per reading, a defect in one included (owner, 2026-09-13; #358's survey).

Out:

- The SDLC itself (`spec/sdlc`, `check-sdlc-tie`): #244's.
- The harness's own settings: the owner's; recorded, not changed.
campaigns.sdlc-alloy:
In:

- `spec/sdlc`, an entity of `spec/` in the shape every other entity has, checked and run in CI the way they are; it opens only what it needs of `spec/campaign`.
- The worker's procedure as an `assuming-role` reference, and the sub-issue kind that carries it.
- A `pre-commit` check that refuses a change whose spec, test and code do not tie.
- Since 2026-09-12 (DECISION on this issue): all of `spec/` -- every `spec/campaign` entity included -- and the scripts, guards and CI that keep it honest, for the simplification chosen there.

Out:

- Sessions outside a campaign: reaching them from `~/.claude` is a successor campaign on dotclaude, filed after this one closes.

request.body:
## Intent

- Owner's order, 2026-09-14, in <campaign>-planner-10's pane: "모든 작업이 완료되었을 시 worker.md 에 worker는 planner에게 sendMessage로 현황을 보고하는 규칙을 하나 넣어" (when all work is done, the worker reports its state to the planner by SendMessage).
- Today `worker.md` step 9 ends at the claim release and sends nothing: the planner learns a worker is finished only from its heartbeat (`campaign-heartbeat.py`), or by reading the pane.

## Definition of done

- `assuming-role/references/worker.md` gains one rule: after step 9 (the release), the worker sends the planner one message by `SendMessage`, carrying what landed (pull request and merge sha, or the closing comment for a sub-issue with no pull request), that its claim is released, and that it is idle with nothing left only on this machine.
- The message carries no fact its GitHub record lacks (`AGENTS.md` § The four messages). If it is none of the four messages, `spec/campaign/orchestration/system.als` and that AGENTS.md table change in the same patch; if it is a `REPORT`, say so in the rule.
- Carried item, NOTE 5658006137 (from pr#409): `worker.md:52` says the `reach` quote goes in the `REPORT`; fold it in or state why it stands.
- A merged pull request, reviewed at its sha.

## Plan

- Run `scripts/campaign-context.py <this issue>` first.
- Read `worker.md` steps 7-9, `AGENTS.md` § The four messages, and the spec's message model before writing; pick the smallest change that keeps the spec and the prose one rule.
- Keep "a finished peer leaves by fact" true: the message is a notification, the leave stays `campaign-close.py`'s.
- Pull request on the first commit; review Opus, level by the size of the diff; REVIEW names model, level and sha.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- Owner's words, 2026-09-14, in <campaign>-planner-10's pane: "worker가 결정을 기다리면 안 돼 planner가 escalation 받으면 결정을 스스로 하던지 아니면 Ask_user_question 해야해" (a worker must not be left waiting: on an escalation the planner decides itself or asks the owner with AskUserQuestion), then "그래 진행해 opus worker로".
- Checked against main 173b93f:
  - `planner.md` step 7 says answer a `BLOCKED` or carry it to the owner, and "never leave one standing", but names no channel to the owner and no moment.
  - `spec/campaign/orchestration/system.als` `decide` lets any session whose `worksOn` holds the issue decide, not only the planner, and has no branch that asks the owner.
  - `checks.als` `BlockedAgentDoesNotProceed` (`expect 1`) admits a worker Waiting forever; nothing rules that trace out.

## Definition of done

- `planner.md` step 7: in the turn a `BLOCKED` arrives, the planner posts the `DECISION` itself, or asks the owner with `AskUserQuestion` and records the answer as the `DECISION`; nothing else runs first.
- The spec: `decide` is the planner's (or the owner's through it), and a check shows a Waiting worker is always answered while its planner is live; a scenario where the planner asks the owner. Strictly simpler on the three counted measures, or equal with the reason stated (a guard on an existing event before a new sig).
- `worker.md` step 4 stays consistent: the worker still stops after its `BLOCKED`.
- A merged pull request, reviewed at its sha; `alloy-check` passes.

## Plan

- Run `scripts/campaign-context.py <this issue>` first.
- Step 1: the spec change and its check; run the affected commands.
- Step 2: `planner.md` step 7; one rule, one home.
- Pull request on the first commit; full review Opus high, REVIEW names model, level and sha; the last `REPORT` at settlement per `worker.md` step 9.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- The owner, 2026-09-14: worker reviews seem to go round in circles in the session histories, and the review procedure may need changing.
- Seen that day: pr#439's narrowed review (Opus low) spent more than 6 minutes and 109k tokens on a diff of one constant and some comments.
- `.claude/skills/assuming-role/references/reviewing.md` says: one full round, then a narrowed one, and a refinement-only round ends the loop. How often practice departs is unmeasured.

## Definition of done

- A measurement `NOTE`: method written before the numbers, window, machine, top rows, full output under `campaign-<campaign>-260909/runtime/`. Per pull request merged on this tracker since 2026-09-01, and per review round:
  - the model and level, tokens, minutes, and the verdict (defect, refinement only, or clean);
  - whether the next push answered the findings.
- Loops flagged, with a count of each kind:
  - a round after a refinement-only verdict;
  - findings that repeat or contradict an earlier round;
  - a narrowed review reading outside its diff;
  - a review re-run with no push between.
- An ideation `NOTE`: an option table opened with purpose and blocker, at least three options, two lenses (rounds and tokens saved; defects missed), each tied to a measured row, one recommendation.
- The owner's pick (options 4 and 3, DECISION issuecomment-5661044487) lands by a pull request on `reviewing.md`, spec with it where a round is modelled; that merge closes this issue.

## Plan

- Driven step by step: post each `NOTE`, then stop for the planner's prompt; `BLOCKED` on any open choice.
- Read `reviewing.md` first, so a departure is judged against the rule.
- Sources:
  - `REVIEW` and `REPORT` comments pinned to a sha, read with `gh`;
  - review subagents' transcripts (`<session>/subagents/`);
  - `scripts/campaign-token-tally.py reviews`: no second reader of what it groups.
- Scratch scripts go under `campaign-<campaign>-260909/scripts/`.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- planner.md step 9 says the planner merges on a worker's `REPORT`. `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions says none of the three conditions names a role. `campaign-roles.py` gives a planner `gh issue` and `gh label` only.
- What the guard does with a planner's `gh pr merge` (`runtime/guard.log`, 2026-09-14):
  - 07:34:03 REFUSED: <campaign>-planner-10, `gh pr merge 32 -R kalaluthien/dotclaude`. The reason: "no claim covering it in a checkout of kalaluthien/dotclaude" (the member rule from <campaign>#389).
  - 07:34:15 allowed: <campaign>-planner-10, `gh pr merge 439`. It passed only because a claim worktree stood under the base root (the unnarrowed fallback), so any claim on this machine would have licensed it.
- So a planner can merge a member repository's pull request only by accident, and cannot merge one at all. Reported by <campaign>-planner-10, who handed pr 32's merge to its worker.

## Definition of done

- One rule for who merges, stated once and enforced by the guard: the planner by role, or the claim's worker.
- It holds for both the base and a member repository.
- `planner.md`, `worker.md` steps 7-9, `campaign-roles.py` and `check-campaign-claim.py` agree, with a guard case for each outcome.
- The fallback no longer licenses a merge by some unrelated claim.

## Plan

- First a `NOTE` comparing two options through two lenses (what a wrong merge costs; how many steps each moves):
  - A: the guard admits a planner's `gh pr merge` when the pull request's head is a claim of the planner's campaign;
  - B: the worker holding the claim merges on the planner's prompt, and planner.md step 9 says so.
- Then stop for the planner's `DECISION` before any code.
- The spec first: `spec/campaign/orchestration/` if a merge's actor is modelled there.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- <campaign>#429 measured reads at 35.5% of tool-result bytes (<campaign>#412). Its option C, grep first and then a bounded range, served:
  - 7 of 7 runs at 9.1% of the bytes (experiment 4, issuecomment-5660485351);
  - 6 of 6 anchored runs at 2.3% (experiment 5, issuecomment-5660796247).
- Review reads scored lower, but every miss lay outside the text read, so a whole read would have missed them too.
- The owner, 2026-09-14: make C the rule for a session's reads, and keep review diffs read whole.
- The rule exists in prose already: `AGENTS.md` § Execution mode says "Read only the part of a file you need", and `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says so too. The bytes show it is not followed, so the prose alone does not hold.

## Definition of done

- A session reading a large file is steered to a grep and a bounded range by something it must consume, not a third copy of the prose.
- A review subagent's diff read is exempt.
- The threshold and the exemption are each stated once, and the check prints what it read and which branch it took.
- A case for each outcome fails first, then passes: steered, exempt, small file.
- The prose copies point at the check, or go.

## Plan

- First a `NOTE` with options, each tied to the #429 numbers and judged by bytes saved and wrong answers risked:
  - a `PreToolUse` hook on `Read` with no range over N lines;
  - a line in the brief hook;

## Intent

- Orchestration still runs on judgments an agent makes by reading: <campaign>#460 counted 217 stated rules in 35 decisions. Each costs turns, is unrecorded, and is made afresh by every session.
- The owner's aim (2026-09-17): Jev (`~/.claude/skills/asking-jev/`) replaces those judgments across the whole process, as the thing the process runs on and not a one-time check of agreement; and the know-how of asking Jev well compounds, so each reading is cheaper and better than the last.
- Code keeps the workflow, exact lookups, refusals, merges and deletes. SDLC readings are <campaign>#458's, on the same caller and registry.

## Definition of done

- One caller, `scripts/campaign-jev.py`: key from `~/.env`, `model` pinned, `unknown` on failure, a state budget, one log line per call.
- One registry: each reading declared once as data — question, `criteria`, state slice, code prefilter, thresholds, tier. No script writes a question inline.
- One corpus: every logged call, joined later to what then happened, is a labelled case; it is the regression suite and the threshold's source.
- A reading replaces the agent's judgment at its moment: tiers `shadow`, `advise`, `act` are the way in, and done is the decision made by Jev with the agent reading only what Jev escalates.
- A lesson lands as a registry change with its failing case and before-and-after numbers, and a general one is also a line in the playbook the next reading's author is handed.
- Every `REPORT` states, of <campaign>#460's text-turning decisions, how many sit at each tier.

| 1 | pr#459: the caller, two readings |
| 2 | the registry, tiers, corpus and its join, and the reader that lists disagreement and drift |
| 3+ | readings by <campaign>#460's ranking, one state group per pull request, each starting at `shadow` |

- The planner drives it; DECISIONs on this issue carry the asking and measuring rules.

## Intent

- The owner asked (2026-09-17) for a wide web survey of how Jev (`~/.claude/skills/asking-jev/`) is used elsewhere, an `awesome-jev` list or anything like it, newest first (2026-09-14 on), and for this system to use what it finds in full.

- Read `topic-web-survey` in the memory pool first.

request.body:
## Intent

- The heartbeat is a poll a planner session must start and answer, so it fails when sessions fail: a planner ran 14 hours with no watch, and one shared-account limit stopped planner and workers together (<campaign>#296 DECISION 5718260714).
- The owner picked option P, sessions push, from <campaign>#296's experiment (its closing DECISION, and the table in NOTEs 5718567952, 5718568276, 5718568611).

## Definition of done

- A merged pull request: a stopped, blocked, full or finished session is handled with no watch running, each row of <campaign>#296's matrix that P answers shown by a test that fails first.
- The watch, its `compact` and `retire` verdicts, and the clock's prose are deleted in the same campaign of work; the drift snapshot stays as a command.
- `campaign-limit-reset.py` stays until `runtime/296/stopfailure.log` shows auto-resume works.

## Plan

- Step 1, a design NOTE, then stop for the planner: which hook carries which event (`Notification` permission prompt, `SessionEnd` read by `reason`, since `/clear` fires it too), how a push finds the planner's pane by name, how it reads back that the prompt became a user turn (<campaign>#296 NOTE 5718552609), where `--autocompact 250k` goes on the launch line, what `install-hooks.sh` installs, the spec delta counted, and the pull request split.
- Step 2, the push hooks and their suite, beside the running watch.
- Step 3, the deletion, once step 2 has run a day without a miss.
- Hooks go in through `install-hooks.sh`; no probe hook is written to `~/.claude/settings.json` by hand.
- A finished worker's own `leave` after its release is P6; the `/exit` queued behind the release's `/compact` is unmeasured, so measure it in step 1.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- <campaign>#381 wants a base for HTML documents, and nobody here can say what current practice is: which forms agents and people now use for docs, views and dashboards, which standards hold in practice, and which principles the forms rest on. The definitions and patterns the campaign will write need that ground first.

## Definition of done

- Every durable finding is a NOTE on this issue, each with its source URL and date, one topic group per NOTE; nothing durable lives only in the directory.
- `<campaign>/survey/README.md` indexes the material: one row per source, with URL, date read, and a one-line takeaway; raw material sits beside it.
- A closing NOTE ranks the candidates for the definitions and patterns sub-issue: which distinctions, which composition patterns, which visualisation rules, each pointing at the findings that support it.
- Closes as completed with no pull request: nothing lands outside the campaign directory and this issue.

## Plan

Planner-driven, one step at a time; each step ends with its NOTE, then the next is prompted.

| step | what | where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the last two months of discussion (2026-07-13 to 2026-09-13) on x.com, arxiv and github: HTML documents by and for agents, agent-facing docs, generated UI, dashboards, artifacts | `survey/recent/` |
| 2 | de facto standards: single-file HTML with CSS and JS, theming, markdown flavours, doc frameworks and their taxonomies, chart and diagram libraries, agent-readable doc conventions | `survey/standards/` |
| 3 | principles: HCI, data visualisation, system and architecture visualisation, hypermedia and HTML application design | `survey/principles/` |
| 4 | synthesis: the closing NOTE | this issue |

- Breadth before depth: a source is a row and a takeaway before it is a study.
- A finding with no source and date is not recorded.
- Read dotclaude's document skills (`show-me` and its kind) before step 2, so standards are measured against what exists.

## Lands in

- none

## Intent

- <campaign>#394 deletes dotclaude's document-kinds spec, its decision-page spec, its hooks and `docs/`, by the owner's word (2026-09-13), and `show-me` is left naming no rule. - One pull request, one full review, narrowed rounds after.

## Intent

- Nothing here states what a good technical document must meet, as a whole or sentence by sentence, so the owner's eye is the only judge; <campaign>#454 found no model to trust with the wording.
- The owner's order (2026-09-17): survey those requirements widely, high level and low level,, then engineer the prompt until Jev judges them well (DECISION 5715463032): a weak number starts the next prompt, it is no verdict. The bar for Jev is the `feedback-jev` memory's.

## Definition of done

- A `NOTE` holds the survey: each requirement with its level (document, section, sentence, figure), source and date, and whether code, a judgment, or only a person can decide it.

- The closing `DECISION` is one table, a row per requirement needing judgment: the best prompt as data and its version, what moved it most, share of good cases still flagged at the threshold flagging every bad one, the code baseline, and the verdict (`shadow` candidate, reject after two designs, person only).

- Step 5, `DECISION` table. Registering a reading (<campaign>#455's registry) is a follow-up.

request.body:
## Intent

- Each phone app (garden, camera today) carries `scripts/release-app.sh` and a `docs/release.md`, but no step reaches the phone: `adb devices` is empty, the phone `R5KL30C9J7B` is intermittent, and "the phone holds the latest release" is never checked. README § Procedures carries it as one planned row.
- Wanted: one procedure for any app with a release script, `app status|release|install <app>`, so what is built, what is released and what the phone runs are three readings of one script.

## Definition of done

- `scripts/app/` carries the three verbs taking an app name; the app list is a host fact (`HOST_APPS`), not a literal in the script; `just --list` names each verb.
- `status <app>` prints the newest `dist/*.apk` in `repos/<app>`, the newest `gh release` tag and asset, and the version the phone reports over `adb -s HOST_PHONE_SERIAL`, each with where it was read; one verdict line, exit 0/1/2, "phone not attached" being exit 2 with the numbered step.
- `release <app>` calls the app's own `scripts/release-app.sh`, never a copy; `install <app>` pushes the released apk, refusing a downgrade without `--force`; a missing clone under `repos/` is cloned.
- Run live on this Mac for garden and camera with `status` output on the pull request; both installed on the phone, or the row names the person's step.
- README row reads `landed`; host record Devices row and `facts.sh` re-probed; `campaign-installed reach` shows the merge at `~/<campaign>`.

## Plan

- Read each app's `docs/release.md` (Scope Out: not edited) and `topic-android-toolchain` for the adb and keystore traps.
- After <campaign>#321, which pins the JDK and adb the release needs.

request.body:
## Intent

- The owner's word, 2026-09-13, in the planner's own pane: "colima restart 도 에이전트가 하도록 허용" — an agent (a script, a Claude session) may restart colima itself.
- Today three places hand it to a person:
  - `AGENTS.md` § stance: "Never: … restart colima …", plus the paragraph carving out `reconcile.sh`'s recovery as the one exception.
  - `lib/service.sh:89-93`: when docker does not answer, `svc_person "docker does not answer" "colima start …"` prints the row instead of starting it.
  - `justfile:102` comment on `reconcile`: "a person's rows are printed, never retried".
- Stopping the herdr server, `tailscale serve reset` and deleting a state directory stay a person's.

## Definition of done

- `AGENTS.md` § stance no longer lists colima among the Never verbs; the reconcile exception paragraph is gone because it is no longer an exception. What stays Never is stated in one line.
- `lib/service.sh`: docker not answering is repaired in place by the same stop-then-start `reconcile.sh` already does (`colima_halt` when `colima status` still reads running, then `colima start`), printing each command and the status line it read; the person's row remains only when the start itself fails.
- One copy of that recovery: `reconcile.sh` calls the `lib/service.sh` form, or the reverse; no second copy.
- `test-host.sh` / `test-reconcile.sh` cover the new branch, and `just reconcile-status` on the live machine reads ok after one run.
- Merged into main; `campaign-installed.py reach` line quoted in the REPORT.

## Plan

- Land after pr#22 (<campaign>#380) merges, since it rewrites `AGENTS.md`; edit the new text.
- Move the recovery out of `reconcile.sh` into `lib/service.sh` and call it from both `reconcile up` and `host.sh check services`.
- Keep `colima stop`'s accepted risk note (a live VM whose docker client is broken is stopped too) next to the code, once.

request.body:
## Intent

- Owner's order (2026-09-13): a reboot of the Mac mini must bring every running service back (tailscale, herdr, colima, Collie, sidecars, the reconcile timer) with no hand, because swap grows over a long uptime (37 days: 3.5 GB swap used, 3.6 GB in the compressor, 12% free) and a reboot is the clean reset only if it is cheap.
- Read on 2026-09-13: no auto-login (`autoLoginUser` unset), so every `gui/501` launch agent -- `sh.brew.colima`, `herdr.collie`, `<campaign>.reconcile`, `<campaign>.wake`, `<campaign>.caffeinate` -- waits for a login; `brew services list` has herdr as `none`; the Tailscale app is not among the login items System Events lists.
- `reconcile.sh up` already revives colima, the Collie bridge and sidecars, and leaves herdr and the tailscale app as a person's rows (a second herdr on the socket is the hazard).

## Definition of done

- A NOTE lists what runs at boot, at login and never, from `launchctl print system`, `gui/501`, login items and `brew services`; then 2-3 designs (auto-login plus launch agents; launch daemons; a boot-time `reconcile up`) through three lenses -- unattended reboot, the herdr socket hazard, the tailscale login -- one recommended; a planner DECISION picks one.
- Landed in `kalaluthien/<campaign>`: the chosen pieces declared under `hosts/hyungs-mac-mini/` and installed by `just host-install`; `just host-check` reads each and says `have:` or `do:`.
- Proved once: a reboot run by the owner, then `just stack-status` reads `VERDICT ok` within the reconcile interval with no hand; the output on the pull request.
- The manual (<campaign>#380) gains a "reboot" row pointing at the verbs.

## Plan

- Step 1: the survey NOTE and the designs; stop.
- Step 2: planner DECISION.
- Step 3: land; the reboot proof is the owner's step, asked for by BLOCKED on this issue.
- Constraints: `reconcile.sh`'s never-steps stay; nothing starts a second herdr server; no `sudo` inside a timer.

## Intent

- Orchestration still runs on judgments an agent makes by reading: <campaign>#460 counted 217 stated rules in 35 decisions. Each costs turns, is unrecorded, and is made afresh by every session.
- The owner's aim (2026-09-17): Jev (`~/.claude/skills/asking-jev/`) replaces those judgments across the whole process, as the thing the process runs on and not a one-time check of agreement; and the know-how of asking Jev well compounds, so each reading is cheaper and better than the last.

## Definition of done

- One caller, `scripts/campaign-jev.py`: key from `~/.env`, `model` pinned, `unknown` on failure, a state budget, one log line per call.

- A lesson lands as a registry change with its failing case and before-and-after numbers, and a general one is also a line in the playbook the next reading's author is handed.

## Intent

- planner.md step 9 says the planner merges on a worker's `REPORT`. `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions says none of the three conditions names a role. `campaign-roles.py` gives a planner `gh issue` and `gh label` only.
- What the guard does with a planner's `gh pr merge` (`runtime/guard.log`, 2026-09-14):
  - 07:34:03 REFUSED: <campaign>-planner-10, `gh pr merge 32 -R kalaluthien/dotclaude`. The reason: "no claim covering it in a checkout of kalaluthien/dotclaude" (the member rule from <campaign>#389).
  - 07:34:15 allowed: <campaign>-planner-10, `gh pr merge 439`. It passed only because a claim worktree stood under the base root (the unnarrowed fallback), so any claim on this machine would have licensed it.
- So a planner can merge a member repository's pull request only by accident, and cannot merge one at all. Reported by <campaign>-planner-10, who handed pr 32's merge to its worker.

## Definition of done

- One rule for who merges, stated once and enforced by the guard: the planner by role, or the claim's worker.
- It holds for both the base and a member repository.
- `planner.md`, `worker.md` steps 7-9, `campaign-roles.py` and `check-campaign-claim.py` agree, with a guard case for each outcome.
- The fallback no longer licenses a merge by some unrelated claim.

## Plan

- First a `NOTE` comparing two options through two lenses (what a wrong merge costs; how many steps each moves):
  - A: the guard admits a planner's `gh pr merge` when the pull request's head is a claim of the planner's campaign;
  - B: the worker holding the claim merges on the planner's prompt, and planner.md step 9 says so.
- Then stop for the planner's `DECISION` before any code.
- The spec first: `spec/campaign/orchestration/` if a merge's actor is modelled there.

request.body:
## Intent

- The `check` job's solver step runs every `spec/**/*.als` serially and is the whole wait on a pull request: run 34646154482 on main at 8778b40 spent 48.1 min in it; every other step under 3 min.
- Two modules are 69% of it: `spec/sdlc/checks.als` 21.8 min, `spec/sdlc/scenarios.als` 11.3 min; then `orchestration/scenarios.als` 8.7, `orchestration/checks.als` 3.9; the other 14 under 2 min together.
- pr#306 widened the sdlc model and a pull request's step went from about 24 to about 58 min; the owner asked on 2026-09-12 that it come down.
- A pull request touching only `scripts/` or one entity still pays for every entity: nothing keys a module's result to its content.

## Definition of done

- On a pull request touching no `spec/` module the step is under 5 min, and on one touching one entity it is bounded by that entity's modules; both measured on a real run, quoted with the run id in the REPORT.
- Every `expect` clause is still enforced on main at every merge: no command is skipped whose module, or a module it opens, changed, and the mechanism says what it read and which modules it ran.
- A per-module solver-time floor is recorded, so the next widening is seen when it lands.
- The pull request is merged and the install shows it.

## Plan

- Measure first: per-module seconds from the run log become a checked-in table or a step output.
- Two levers, in order; add the second only if the first misses the target:
  1. Run an entity's modules only when its content, or a module it `open`s, differs from the last green main run: key on a hash of the closure, never on the git diff, and run everything on main.
  2. Fan the step out into a matrix job per entity so the wall time is the slowest entity, not the sum.
- Shrinking the sdlc scopes is a model change for a sub-issue of its own; this one changes no `.als`.
- Constraint: the snapshot step, `alloy-check.py`'s dead-event refusal and `check-merge-review.py`'s step stay.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- A worker that authored a pull request launches its own review subagent (reviewing.md, feedback-review-roles) and posts the `REVIEW` it returns. Claude Code's auto-mode permission check refuses that `gh pr comment` as self-approval: tidy-dotclaude#413 BLOCKED, 2026-09-14, dotclaude pr#30 at b83e9c1, no findings, unposted. Merge condition 1 then cannot be met from the worker's pane.
- Owner (tidy-dotclaude#413 DECISION, 2026-09-14): it happens often; <campaign> designs the fix. The interim is a fresh reviewer session per pull request, one launch each.
- The refusal is the harness's, not this tree's guard (`check-campaign-claim.py` refuses no `REVIEW` post); the classifier reads the session, not the subagent.

## Definition of done

- A `DECISION` here with 2-3 options judged by three lenses -- what the harness classifier sees, what merge condition 2 (a reviewer that wrote no commit) still guarantees, and the cost per pull request -- and one recommendation. Candidates at least: the review subagent posts the comment itself; a reviewer session the planner launches once and reuses; the `REVIEW` written to a file and posted by a script or a workflow the classifier does not read as the author.
- Evidence: a live probe per option on a throwaway pull request, quoting the refusal or the posted comment URL; a count of refusals on this machine's transcripts (`self-approval` in tool_result) so the "often" is a number.
- The DECISION names follow-ups, one mechanism each; this issue closes with no pull request.

## Plan

- Read reviewing.md, feedback-review-roles, `check-campaign-claim.py`'s `--report` path, and tidy-dotclaude#413's two comments.
- Count the refusals; run the three probes on one throwaway pull request on the base; post the DECISION and file follow-ups.

## Lands in

- none

request.body:
## Intent

- Three guards keep a set of zero files: `check-tree-shape.py` R7 (`docs/`, never judged a file), `check-cross-references.py`'s `.html` branch (23 lines), and `check.yml`'s solver floors, which warn and never refuse. `alloy-check.py --digest` is called by nothing.
- Four spec rules are prose only: "each entity is N files", "`system.als` declares no command", "each entity opens the one below", "spec normative / docs not".
- The HTML question decided 2026-09-12: an `.html` under `spec/<entity>/` is admitted only as a Spec artifact tied by name -- every `<section data-scenario data-refines>` names a live command of its own entity and a suite witnesses it -- and the base carries zero such files, no runner, no CI step.

## Definition of done

- One merged pull request: R7, the xref `.html` branch, the floors table and budget warning, and `--digest` deleted; `check-tree-shape.py` refuses an entity that is not exactly `system.als` + `checks.als`, with its named failing case; `alloy-check.py --commands` refuses a command declared in a `system.als`, and joins `pre-commit`.
- `check-sdlc-tie.py`'s `DECL` becomes a two-entry table (`.als`, `.html`); T6 reads `data-refines` as it reads `# witnesses:`; T7 refuses an `.html` under `spec/` declaring no scenario or one no suite witnesses; each with a failing case. `spec/sdlc/system.als` gains `sig Html in Artifact` and `refines` in `AddsShape`'s place.
- `check.yml`: one guards step, ten solve jobs, its cache-key comment true. AGENTS.md § The three planes loses the docs/ row; README § Reading order says two files per entity.

## Plan

- Lands after the campaign moves sub-issue, so the shape guard is true of the tree on the day it lands.
- One commit per script; the HTML rule is its own commit, with the model change beside its reader.
- Off limits: predicate bodies in `spec/campaign/**` (the fixes sub-issue).

request.body:
## Intent

- The SDLC has been exercised only on itself: every sub-issue of <campaign>#244 changed `spec/sdlc`, the procedure, the view or the guard. Nothing shows an ordinary program — users, state, a runtime — going from intent to code under `landing-a-change.md`, or where the procedure bends when the code is not Alloy and the test is not an `expect`.
- The owner's ask (2026-09-10): at least one general piece of software (a garden planner, a camera app, or the like) developed under the <campaign> procedure and then verified against it.

## Definition of done

- One program of the owner's choosing, in a repository named in <campaign>#244's `## Repos`, built from intent through plan, `spec/` (an Alloy model with scenarios and checks), a view, tests that failed first, and code — each stage's artifact named in the `REPORT`, every scenario tied to a test and a code path as `check-sdlc-tie.py` reads them.
- The program runs on one real input end to end, and the `REPORT` shows it.
- Every place the procedure bent — a stage that did not fit, a criterion that misjudged, a tie the guard could not read outside the base — is a `NOTE` on this issue, and each becomes an item on the next sub-issue touching `spec/sdlc` or the reference.
- The pull request merged in that repository, closing this issue with the full name.

## Plan

- Before any work: the owner names the program and its repository; adding the repository to `## Repos` is a scope change, synced at that moment (`opening-campaign`, "A repository the campaign issue's `## Repos` list does not name"), and it replaces `- none` there and in `## Lands in` below.
- Worked by a herdr delegate in the clone, `development` profile, `--add-dir <base>` so the guards reach the clone.
- Keep the program small enough that the spec is the largest artifact; the point is the procedure, not the product.
- Constraint: `spec/sdlc` is not edited from this branch; a bend is a `NOTE`, never a local fix.

- none
